headline_marked: [[ZeroTrace launches]] an air-gapped, local-first AI copilot for zero-day behavioral SOC
headline: ZeroTrace launches an air-gapped, local-first AI copilot for zero-day behavioral SOC
summary: ZeroTrace is an AI-assisted, local-first cybersecurity incident triage copilot designed for developers and small teams, offering privacy-conscious investigation of suspicious runtime behavior.
details: ZeroTrace is a new AI-assisted cybersecurity incident triage copilot, built for independent DevOps engineers, freelancers, and small infrastructure teams. It helps investigate suspicious runtime behavior without the complexity and cost of enterprise solutions.

Unlike traditional EDRs that rely on static hashes, ZeroTrace uses pure behavioral provenance reasoning. It ingests raw kernel and process execution telemetry to autonomously deduce adversary intent in real time.

The system leverages a locally hosted, GPU-accelerated Gemma 4 model (zerotrace-analyst) for incident analysis, risk assessment, and investigation workflows. This air-gapped approach keeps sensitive telemetry under user control.

By using a local open-weight language model via Ollama, ZeroTrace reduces recurring inference costs and limits exposure of security data to third-party AI providers. This makes intelligent security triage more accessible and affordable.

The project aims to simplify security investigation, review, and documentation through a dedicated SOC dashboard. It provides risk scores as triage indicators, which are designed to be evaluated alongside supporting evidence by a human operator.

ZeroTrace is open-source, with its repository containing source code and implementation details for exploration and contribution. It combines modern web technologies with security telemetry and local AI for a privacy-conscious approach.

headline_marked: [[Anthropic's Claude Code Review is GA]] but never fails a PR, unlike their internal policy
headline: Anthropic's Claude Code Review is GA but never fails a PR, unlike their internal policy
summary: While Anthropic's own repos block merges on Claude Code findings, the commercial product deliberately doesn't, leaving enforcement to the user.
details: Anthropic has officially launched Claude Code Review, its AI-powered code review product, out of research preview. However, a notable difference exists between how Anthropic uses the tool internally and how the commercial product functions for customers.

Internally, Anthropic's own Claude Code repositories block pull requests if any bug or security review finding is open. In contrast, the commercial Claude Code Review product "never approves or blocks your pull request, and the check run never concludes as a failure."

This is a deliberate design choice; the product posts findings, not approvals, and users are responsible for configuring their repositories to block merges based on these findings. The service is now available to Claude Team and Enterprise organizations.

Admins can choose "Quick, Standard (default), or Deep" review levels for each repository. Most reviews are now significantly faster, completing in 6-10 minutes, a 3x improvement over the preview phase.

The review process involves multiple agents reading code diffs in parallel, followed by a verification pass to eliminate false positives. Findings are presented as inline comments and in a check run, tagged as Important, Nit, or Pre-existing.
Claude Code Review operates on Anthropic's infrastructure with read-only access and does not build or run user code. It currently works exclusively with GitHub repositories.

The service is not available to organizations utilizing Zero Data Retention, HIPAA configurations, or customer-managed encryption keys. Users on any plan can still run /code-review locally within a Claude Code session.

Anthropic states that Claude writes about 90% of Claude Code's own codebase. They also claim that from June to September, merged pull requests to their codebase more than doubled, while reverts fell by over 40%, though these numbers lack independent verification.

The ultimate goal for Anthropic's internal process is for most PRs to merge with at most one human in the loop, potentially the author, without increasing reverts or incidents. They employ rules like "The change sets the tier, not the author" and "Whoever prompted the change is on the hook for it."

Users who wish to block merges based on Claude Code Review findings have two main options. The first is to enable GitHub's branch protection rule requiring all conversations on a pull request to be resolved, as findings are posted as inline threads.

The second option involves gating on "Important" findings only. This requires a custom pre-merge script that parses the machine-readable output from the Claude Code Review check run to identify and block merges if critical findings remain open.
